findings.checklist_item: Specify that the fold AND the ref move execute inside a SINGLE held write-lock window (widen the lock to span `_fold_heads` + the ref move, or move the ref-move into `_fold_heads`'s lock scope), and give the on-branch case a compare-and-swap equivalent (e.g. `git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip>` then `git reset --hard`, or verify the tip is unchanged before `reset --hard`) so a concurrent mover aborts rather than being clobbered.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'publish the folded sha onto refs/heads/<ref> under the same lock'
s3_doctor.py:239 `with _lock.write_lock(...)` is scoped to `_fold_heads`; `_heal_locked` calls `_fold_heads` then `_publish_and_prune` as separate un-shared-lock calls (s3_doctor.py:142-143)
Plan step 2 gives CAS only to the off-branch update-ref: 'git reset --hard <merged>' for the on-branch case names no old-tip precondition
findings.finding: The plan's ref-move step (step 2) is claimed to run 'under the same lock' as the fold, but the write lock (`_lock.write_lock`) is currently acquired INSIDE `_fold_heads` (s3_doctor.py:239) and released when it returns; step 2 runs in `_heal_locked` after `_fold_heads` returns, so the fold's tip-read and the ref move are in separate lock windows. Moreover the on-branch `git reset --hard <merged>` has no compare-and-swap (unlike the off-branch `update-ref <merged> <old-tip>`), so a concurrent writer that advances `refs/heads/<ref>` between the in-lock fold and the reset is silently clobbered — re-introducing the silent-loss class this ticket exists to close.
findings.location: Plan step 2 (`_heal_locked`, s3_doctor.py:136-143); step 1 lock at s3_doctor.py:239
scenarios: On-branch heal races a concurrent tickets push that advances refs/heads/<ref> after the fold reads the tip; reset --hard drops the concurrent commit
Fold and ref-move span separate write-lock acquisitions, allowing an interleaved writer between them
findings.suggested_fix: Perform both the fold and the ref publish inside one `_lock.write_lock` acquisition; for the on-branch case do the CAS `update-ref ... <old-tip>` first (aborting on mismatch) and only then `git reset --hard <merged>` to sync index/worktree, matching the off-branch atomicity guarantee.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the write lock serializes all cross-process mutation of refs/heads/<ref>, or make the on-branch path also compare-and-swap old-tip before reset --hard so a concurrent mover aborts the heal rather than being clobbered.
evidence: 'git reset --hard <merged>, so index and worktree stay consistent'
off-branch: 'git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip> — a compare-and-swap, so a concurrent mover aborts the heal instead of clobbering'
the plan asymmetrically protects only the off-branch path against concurrent movers
findings.finding: On-branch publish uses `git reset --hard <merged>` with no compare-and-swap old-value guard, unlike the off-branch path which uses `git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip>` explicitly to make a concurrent mover abort. The plan does not state whether the write lock serializes cross-process ref mutation; if it only serializes within the doctor, an on-branch concurrent advance of the ref would be silently clobbered by reset --hard.
scenarios: Another process advances refs/heads/<ref> between the fold-tip read and the on-branch reset --hard, under a lock that does not cover that mover.
findings.suggested_fix: On-branch, first `git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip>` (CAS) and only then `git reset --hard <merged>` to sync worktree/index; abort if the CAS fails.

findings.checklist_item: State explicitly which tree merge-tree reads the `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` `.gitattributes` line from (and confirm the throwaway experiment placed that file in the same relative tree position as a real tracker), so the merge=ours equivalence claim is grounded against the ort-vs-recursive attribute-source difference rather than an incidental property of the probe repo.
evidence: Plan: 'git merge-tree --write-tree A B DOES honour the tracker's configured `ours` driver (merge.ours.driver=true...) together with the tickets-branch .gitattributes .bridge_state/* merge=ours line ... produced a tree byte-identical to the worktree git merge on the same inputs'

Retrieved web source (github.com/afrimberger/mergedriver-test) states of merge-tree behaviour: 'ort doesn't respect HEAD:.gitattributes, but recursive does' — merge-tree uses the ort strategy while worktree `git merge` historically used recursive, so which tree's .gitattributes is consulted is not automatically equivalent
AC line: '.bridge_state/* merge=ours still resolves derived-file collisions in the fold' depends directly on this attribute-source being correct
findings.finding: The plan's central 'experimentally settled' claim that `git merge-tree --write-tree` honours the tracker's `merge=ours` driver may not have pinned down WHICH `.gitattributes` source merge-tree consults, and the ort strategy backing merge-tree reads attributes differently from the recursive strategy used by the worktree `git merge` it replaces.
findings.location: Plan → 'Mechanism decision', first bullet ('git merge-tree --write-tree A B DOES honour the tracker's configured ours driver ... byte-identical to the worktree git merge')
